items.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022
items.q: you also hear the drummer do something or Ron last night playing the organ, okay the way he chorded it, or like that connection you have, the conversation

ctx.x: Well thank you for the kind words. It was a really cool place to play actually, The Other Side, and it was a nice gallery with art work and stuff. And then it was filled with people but with 60 — it was like packed but it’s a small place. But really, talking to people before, during the break and then afterwards really, it’s a kind of a cool thing about jazz or this improvised music is that those people were there to really hear music and they stayed, and then talking to them and just you realize that this music…

Then you have to just allow the music to happen. And that’s what’s the beautiful part about improvised music and jazz is that then you also hear the drummer do something or Ron last night playing the organ, okay the way he chorded it, or like that connection you have, the conversation. So then it’s a combination of like accepting what’s coming in, accepting what’s happening around you, and then the feeling of the room, actually when you kind of just sense the vibes from the people. There’s all that combination it…

It was clear to me that you understand the importance and the power of space and dynamics. Because there was a number of times, one time when you were playing — you played the melody to “Bye-Bye Blackbird.” And there was all those like holes in there. And you know Ron was playing a little bit behind you but I don’t hear people do that that much. And I wonder why you did it and I wondered is it because of this audience — it’s very quiet in there. And those silences, man, are very —
